ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy SHA 7f3a92c introduced a Puppet manifest change to manifests/dns/nameserver.pp that updated the authoritative nameserver (named-auth) IP from 10.0.1.53 to 10.0.2.53 and correctly triggered a Service[named-auth] restart, but omitted the corresponding notify/subscribe relationship for Service[named-cache]. As a result, named-cache continued forwarding queries to the old IP 10.0.1.53, causing SERVFAIL for all internal hostnames. The emergency remediation Puppet run then executed Exec[rebuild-zone-file] via build-zone.py, which itself attempted to resolve provisioning-api.internal.svc through the still-broken named-cache, received SERVFAIL, wrote an empty zone file, and reloaded named-auth with 0 records, escalating SERVFAILs to NXDOMAINs for all internal services. Concurrently, repeated Puppet runs spawned hundreds of unreaped build-zone.py child processes that exhausted memory on fileservers, preventing SSH access and extending the incident to 1h35m.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately restore the last known-good zone file backup (serial 2024031401) to /etc/named/zones/internal.svc.zone and reload named-auth to fix NXDOMAIN. 2. Restart named-cache with forwarder explicitly set to 10.0.2.53 bypassing Puppet. 3. Kill zombie build-zone.py processes on fileservers via out-of-band console to recover memory and restore SSH. 4. Patch manifests/dns/nameserver.pp to add a notify => Service[named-cache] relationship alongside Service[named-auth] in the IP-change resource block. 5. Fix build-zone.py to use direct IP for the provisioning API rather than DNS lookup, preventing circular dependency during DNS outages. 6. Add Puppet exec timeout and process reaping to zone_rebuild.pp to prevent zombie accumulation.
